evaluatedBaseline: NCI + Prism Central + LCM + Flow + NCM/Self-Service + Move + NKP + Nutanix DR (public product capability baseline, 2026-08)
disclaimer: Parity judgments are SME-style mappings of public Nutanix product capabilities to CN v0.3 FeatureIDs for workshop dry-run. Evidence URLs are public product/docs pages. Exact AOS/AHV/Prism point releases still require customer portal validation. Partial rows include workaround notes.

VCF-01-F01.notes: Prism Central provides multi-cluster inventory, topology, and capacity visibility across registered clusters.

VCF-01-F02.workaround: Use cluster create/expand/destroy workflows instead of VCF Workload Domains.
VCF-01-F02.technicalImpact: No 1:1 Workload Domain construct; operational model differs from SDDC Manager domains.
VCF-01-F02.notes: Nutanix manages clusters, not VCF-style workload domains.

VCF-01-F03.notes: Cluster expand/contract and node add/remove are core NCI operations.

VCF-01-F04.workaround: Separate management via Prism Element vs Prism Central and RBAC/projects; not identical to VCF management domain.
VCF-01-F04.technicalImpact: Isolation model differs; governance must be redesigned.
VCF-01-F04.notes: PE/PC separation is analogous but not equivalent to VCF principal/workload domains.

VCF-01-F05.notes: Host imaging/commissioning via Foundation and lifecycle tooling.

VCF-01-F06.workaround: Use NCM configuration/ops policies and Prism desired configuration where licensed.
VCF-01-F06.technicalImpact: Baseline/drift semantics differ from VCF configuration baselines.
VCF-01-F06.notes: Configuration governance available but not SDDC Manager baseline parity.

VCF-01-F07.workaround: Use AHV Metro / stretch and site-aware DR constructs.
VCF-01-F07.technicalImpact: Site affinity and failure-domain UX differs from VCF stretch domain model.

VCF-02-F01.workaround: Use Foundation bring-up instead of VCF Installer wizard.
VCF-02-F01.technicalImpact: Different bring-up UX and prerequisite model.
VCF-02-F01.notes: Initial cluster bring-up exists; not VCF Installer.

VCF-02-F02.notes: No SDDC Manager equivalent. LCM upgrades components but does not orchestrate VCF-style domain workflows.

VCF-02-F03.workaround: Use LCM inventory/depot and dark-site bundle workflows.
VCF-02-F03.technicalImpact: Bundle formats and depot model differ from VCF depot.
VCF-02-F03.notes: LCM manages update inventory; not VCF bundle schema.

VCF-02-F04.notes: LCM performs upgrade prechecks and dependency handling.

VCF-02-F05.notes: LCM coordinates one-click software/firmware upgrades across cluster nodes.

VCF-02-F06.workaround: Select component update sets in LCM; selective deferral depends on LCM recommendations.
VCF-02-F06.technicalImpact: Skip-level policy model differs from VCF selective update controls.
VCF-02-F06.notes: Selective updates possible but not VCF skip-level controls.

VCF-02-F07.workaround: Retain LCM/Prism upgrade history; rollback is often re-image/reinstall constrained.
VCF-02-F07.technicalImpact: Rollback posture typically weaker than customer expectation for full stack rollback.
VCF-02-F07.notes: History available; rollback constraints must be documented per release.

VCF-03-F01.notes: AHV provides enterprise VM compute services.

VCF-03-F02.notes: Prism Central is the multi-cluster management plane with RBAC and APIs.

VCF-03-F03.notes: AHV Dynamic Scheduling / placement and maintenance evacuation are supported.

VCF-03-F04.notes: AHV HA restarts VMs on host failure.

VCF-03-F05.workaround: Use VM/categories/project quotas and scheduling policies instead of classic vSphere resource pools.
VCF-03-F05.technicalImpact: Resource-pool semantics are not identical to vSphere.
VCF-03-F05.notes: Controls exist via categories/projects; not 1:1 resource pools.

VCF-03-F06.notes: VM provision, clone, snapshot/revert are core AHV operations.

VCF-03-F07.notes: Maintenance mode and live migration (AHV) supported.

VCF-04-F01.notes: AOS provides distributed shared storage containers for VMs.

VCF-04-F02.notes: Storage policies/RF and container policies map to SPBM-like intent.

VCF-04-F03.notes: Compression/dedup/erasure coding efficiency features available on AOS.

VCF-04-F04.notes: Replication Factor / fault tolerance and rebuild are core AOS capabilities.

VCF-04-F05.workaround: Use Metro Availability / synchronous replication with witness.
VCF-04-F05.technicalImpact: Stretch design and witness requirements differ from vSAN stretch.
VCF-04-F05.notes: Metro supported with specific topology requirements.

VCF-04-F06.workaround: Add Nutanix Files and/or Volumes for file/block supplemental services.
VCF-04-F06.technicalImpact: Separate product packaging vs integrated vSAN File Services.
VCF-04-F06.notes: File services via Files product; not identical to vSAN File Services.

VCF-04-F07.notes: Health checks, support bundles, and rebuild/resync visibility available.

VCF-05-F01.notes: Managed subnets/segments and VPC constructs available with Flow Virtual Networking.

VCF-05-F02.workaround: Use VPC routing/NAT/VPN constructs; map Tier-0/1 designs to Flow VPC model.
VCF-05-F02.notes: SDN routing exists; taxonomy differs from NSX.

VCF-05-F03.workaround: Use Flow gateways/NAT and partner service insertion for advanced edge services.
VCF-05-F03.technicalImpact: Edge node model not identical to NSX Edge.
VCF-05-F03.notes: Gateway/NAT/VPN style services available; advanced LB may need partners.

VCF-05-F04.notes: VPC multi-tenancy networking is a primary Flow Virtual Networking capability.

VCF-05-F05.workaround: Validate underlay with Nutanix networking best practices; overlay via Flow VPC.
VCF-05-F05.technicalImpact: Overlay/underlay troubleshooting model differs from NSX transport zones.

VCF-05-F06.workaround: Use managed DHCP in AHV/Flow; DNS often external or integrated services.
VCF-05-F06.technicalImpact: DNS/IPAM depth may be less than NSX.

VCF-05-F07.workaround: Use Prism/Flow topology and alerts; advanced path tracing may need packet capture tooling.
VCF-05-F07.technicalImpact: Observability depth below mature NSX Traceflow in some scenarios.

VCF-06-F01.workaround: Implement microsegmentation with Flow Network Security policies/categories.
VCF-06-F01.technicalImpact: Policy model differs from NSX Distributed Firewall.
VCF-06-F01.notes: Microsegmentation available; not NSX DFW feature parity.

VCF-06-F02.workaround: Use VPC/gateway security policies and perimeter controls.
VCF-06-F02.technicalImpact: North-south controls exist but differ from NSX gateway firewall.

VCF-06-F03.notes: Categories/dynamic grouping are a core Nutanix policy construct.

VCF-06-F04.workaround: Use Flow advanced security options and/or service insertion with partners for IDS/IPS-class controls.
VCF-06-F04.technicalImpact: May require partner stack for NSX IDS/IPS equivalent.
VCF-06-F04.notes: Native advanced threat depth varies by license/partner.

VCF-06-F05.workaround: Combine identity sources with categories/RBAC; context-aware depth may be limited.
VCF-06-F05.technicalImpact: Identity-aware firewall parity incomplete vs NSX.
VCF-06-F05.notes: Some context controls; not full NSX identity firewall.

VCF-06-F06.workaround: Use change control process + policy versioning practices in Prism/Flow.
VCF-06-F06.notes: Policy lifecycle exists with operational process differences.

VCF-06-F07.workaround: Export policy inventories and compliance reports from Flow/NCM.
VCF-06-F07.technicalImpact: Compliance evidence packs differ from NSX reporting.

VCF-07-F01.notes: Infrastructure metrics, dashboards, and alerts are core Prism capabilities.

VCF-07-F02.workaround: Use NCM ops/logging integrations or SIEM (Splunk/ELK) for deep log analytics.
VCF-07-F02.technicalImpact: May need external log platform vs Aria Operations for Logs.
VCF-07-F02.notes: Log analysis often hybrid with external SIEM.

VCF-07-F03.notes: Capacity planning and what-if style insights available in NCM/Prism.

VCF-07-F04.workaround: Use NCM security/config compliance features where licensed.
VCF-07-F04.technicalImpact: Compliance content packs differ from Aria.
VCF-07-F04.notes: Configuration/compliance monitoring available with licensing caveats.

VCF-07-F05.workaround: Map apps via categories/projects and NCM app discovery where available.
VCF-07-F05.technicalImpact: App dependency mapping may be less deep than Aria.

VCF-07-F06.notes: Alert policies and notification routing supported.

VCF-08-F01.technicalImpact: Catalog UX and governance differ from Aria Automation.

VCF-08-F02.notes: Blueprints/templates with parameters are core Calm/Self-Service capability.

VCF-08-F03.workaround: Configure approval policies in Self-Service / projects.
VCF-08-F03.technicalImpact: Approval depth/ITSM-native flows may need integration work.
VCF-08-F03.notes: Approvals supported; governance maturity depends on design.

VCF-08-F04.notes: Day-2 actions and runbooks supported in blueprints.

VCF-08-F05.notes: Projects/tenancy and entitlements are standard NCM constructs.

VCF-08-F06.workaround: Integrate via REST APIs/webhooks to ServiceNow/pipelines.
VCF-08-F06.technicalImpact: Out-of-box ITSM connectors less turnkey than some Aria packs.

VCF-08-F07.notes: Extensibility via APIs, custom actions, credential management supported.

VCF-09-F01.workaround: Use NKP for Kubernetes cluster lifecycle on NCI.
VCF-09-F01.technicalImpact: Not vSphere Supervisor / VKS identical model.
VCF-09-F01.notes: K8s lifecycle via NKP, not VKS Supervisor.

VCF-09-F02.notes: Namespaces, quotas, and tenancy controls available in Kubernetes platforms.

VCF-09-F03.workaround: Use CNI + Flow/VPC integration patterns for cluster networking.
VCF-09-F03.notes: Pod/service networking supported; SDN integration differs.

VCF-09-F04.notes: Persistent volumes via Nutanix CSI/data services for Kubernetes.

VCF-09-F05.workaround: Integrate Harbor/Quay or managed registry with NKP.
VCF-09-F05.technicalImpact: Registry may be external add-on vs integrated VCF package.
VCF-09-F05.notes: Registry typically integrated, not always bundled identically.

VCF-09-F06.workaround: Apply PSS/PodSecurity, secrets managers, and admission policies in NKP.
VCF-09-F06.technicalImpact: Security pack composition differs from VKS.
VCF-09-F06.notes: Platform security controls available with configuration effort.

VCF-09-F07.workaround: Provide developer self-service via NKP UI/CLI/API and GitOps.
VCF-09-F07.technicalImpact: Developer UX differs from VKS/Tanzu experience.

VCF-10-F01.notes: Move supports cold/seeded migrations into AHV.

VCF-10-F02.workaround: Use Move cutover and Cross-Cluster Live Migration where supported for running workloads.
VCF-10-F02.technicalImpact: Not identical to HCX vMotion fabric; network continuity constraints apply.
VCF-10-F02.notes: Live mobility options exist with constraints vs HCX.

VCF-10-F04.workaround: Plan IP changes or use network extension patterns carefully; HCX-style L2 extension is not 1:1.
VCF-10-F04.technicalImpact: Network extension is a common HCX strength; expect redesign.
VCF-10-F04.notes: L2 extension parity limited vs HCX.

VCF-10-F05.workaround: Import/migrate existing estates with Move; converge operationally under Prism Central.
VCF-10-F05.notes: Import/converge is process+Move, not VCF workflow.

VCF-10-F06.workaround: Use Move migration plans/waves and project tracking.
VCF-10-F06.notes: Wave planning supported with operational process.

VCF-10-F07.workaround: Keep source powered until validation; define rollback windows before cutover.

VCF-11-F01.workaround: Use snapshots/replication plus partner backup (HYCU, Veeam, Commvault) for full backup estates.
VCF-11-F01.technicalImpact: Enterprise backup often partner-based vs built-in VCF backup product.
VCF-11-F01.notes: Protection available; backup ecosystem is hybrid.

VCF-11-F02.workaround: Restore via DR recovery plans and/or partner backup restore workflows.
VCF-11-F02.technicalImpact: File-level restore depends on partner tool.

VCF-11-F03.notes: Entity-centric DR with protection policies and recovery plans is a Nutanix product capability.

VCF-11-F04.notes: RPO policy configuration and monitoring supported in protection policies.

VCF-11-F05.workaround: Design immutable/partner cyber-recovery patterns; validate license/features.
VCF-11-F05.technicalImpact: Cyber recovery maturity depends on partner + design.

VCF-11-F06.workaround: Use app-consistent partner agents for databases.

VCF-11-F07.notes: DR test/failover reporting and protection status available.

VCF-12-F01.workaround: Enable GPU passthrough/vGPU on AHV and/or GPT-in-a-Box offerings.
VCF-12-F01.technicalImpact: Not identical to VCF Private AI Services packaging.

VCF-12-F02.workaround: Deploy model serving on NKP/GPU nodes or GPT-in-a-Box stack.
VCF-12-F02.technicalImpact: Private AI productization differs from VCF Private AI Services.
VCF-12-F02.notes: Model hosting possible; not turnkey VCF Private AI parity.

VCF-12-F03.workaround: Assemble RAG pipelines with platform storage + partner AI stack.
VCF-12-F03.notes: Data pipeline/RAG not a single built-in VCF-equivalent product.

VCF-12-F04.notes: No first-class MLOps lifecycle equivalent to VCF Private AI Services MLOps claims in this baseline.

VCF-12-F05.workaround: Use projects/RBAC and platform policy to govern AI resource access.

VCF-12-F06.workaround: Run AI workloads on AHV using platform identity/network/storage/ops.
VCF-12-F06.technicalImpact: Integration is DIY vs packaged VCF Private AI.
VCF-12-F06.notes: Platform integration possible at infrastructure layer.

VCF-12-F07.workaround: Keep inference on-prem; control egress via network policy.
VCF-12-F07.notes: Private on-prem posture achievable with controls.
